# PathwaySeeker

> PathwaySeeker lets an AI assistant (Claude Code, Codex or any MCP client) answer questions about metabolic pathways using a scientist's own proteomics and metabolomics data. It builds an organism-specific graph of compounds, reactions and enzymes from the measurements (KEGG identifiers), checks every step of a proposed pathway against that graph, and labels each step as supported by the data or as a hypothesis. Published as a bioRxiv preprint (2026) by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory.

## Start here
- [README](https://github.com/pnnl/PathwaySeeker/blob/master/README.md): what it does, five-minute setup, using your own data
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/pnnl/PathwaySeeker/blob/master/AGENTS.md): step-by-step setup instructions for AI assistants
- [Skill](https://github.com/pnnl/PathwaySeeker/blob/master/skills/pathwayseeker/SKILL.md): how an assistant builds graphs and answers questions

## Reference
- [Paper data](https://github.com/pnnl/PathwaySeeker/blob/master/paper/README.md): training data, evaluation queries, scoring rubric and results
- [Preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.04.14.718256v1): PathwaySeeker: Evidence-Grounded AI Reasoning over Organism-Specific Metabolic Networks
